acceptance: The owner's choice is recorded in this item's context.
Test: a member that adds a new test file and the regenerated _project/inert-doc-readers.json lands (option 1 or 2) or is refused with a message naming the registration rule (option 3).
Test: a hand-edited generated index that differs from a fresh regeneration is refused at landing.
The list of generated files and their generator commands lives in one place and the docs link to it.
description:
## Problem
A registered batch freezes each member's path scope, and a leader fix must stay inside the union of member scopes. Some repository files are generated indexes that any member can make stale, for example _project/inert-doc-readers.json, which changes when a new test file reads a document. On 2026-11-24 a release-readiness member added a test, its check failed on tests/unit/scripts/test_inert_paths.py ("inert-doc-readers.json is stale"), and neither the member nor the leader could land the regenerated file. The only exits were dropping the test or aborting the batch; the owner chose to abort three batches and deliver them as ordinary PRs.

## Decision gate (owner)
Options: (1) batch tooling treats a fixed, named set of generated files as always landable when the leader regenerates them with their generator and the result matches a fresh regeneration; (2) register_batch adds those files to every scope automatically; (3) document that batches must list them in scope at registration. Recommendation: (1). Record the owner's choice in this item before implementation.

## Change
Implement the chosen option in scripts/batch_integration.py (scope check at land and at batch-advance), list the generated files and their generator commands in one place, and document it in docs/agent/batch-feature-delivery.md.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create), never the primary clone; heavy test runs only through lock-taking entry points; never set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK or force admission; stage explicit paths; add a changelog.d fragment if users can see the change; no explanatory comments (make comment-policy-check). A hand-edited generated file must still be refused; only byte-identical regeneration is accepted.
